messages:
sam-incident-bot: Incident alert — HIGH latency observed in hosted inference cluster (us-east-1). p95 has spiked to ~1.8s, p50 up to ~400ms. Alert: INF-LAT-USE1-001. Auto-escalation to oncall.
elena-oncall: I'm looking. paging myself @channel. Saw the alert at 09:02 UTC. Checking dashboards and recent deploys.
ryan-sre: I can join. Any errors in runtime logs or OOMs?
elena-oncall: No OOMs in GPU nodes. CPU on control plane instances normal. Throughput dropped on a subset of model endpoints — looks like sustained token processing slowdown. Backends returning 200 but token generation slower.
alex-engr: Rolling logs: seeing repeated slow kernel-fallback in inference runtime for int8 paths. A few nodes show increased kernel switch latency.
maya-pm: Which customers are impacted? Need to prepare a short external note.
elena-oncall: Preliminary scope: ~8% of hosted requests in us-east-1 routed to affected pool. No errors, just higher latency. Will confirm customer list with support query.
support-bot: Query run: 12 active orgs with elevated p95 in the timeframe. Small cohort (mostly prod traffic from startups + two enterprise tests). I'll DM the account owners and hold for template.
ryan-sre: Quick mitigation options: 1) Drain affected nodes and failover to warm pool (adds cold-start latency for some requests) 2) Switch routing policy to prefer a different model variant (lower precision) with faster kernel path 3) Autoscale more capacity (may be slower than immediate failover).
elena-oncall: I'm going to start a canary routing change: route 20% of traffic away from the affected node pool to the warm pool. If p95 improves, we can ramp.
ops-lead: +1. Keep canary small and watch SLOs. Notify customers if we escalate to larger shift.
statuspage-bot: Draft statuspage update ready for approval: "We are investigating increased latency affecting a subset of requests in US‑East. Customers may experience slower responses for text generation. Engineers are actively mitigating. Next update in 30 minutes or as events occur." (needs ETA + impact windows)
elena-oncall: Approving draft with ETA estimate: recovery expected within 30–90 minutes depending on failover behavior. Update: starting canary at 09:07 UTC.
alex-engr: Canary in flight. Monitoring tail latencies. Logs show kernel fallback rate decreased for routed traffic but some residual slow traces.
ryan-sre: Observed p95 drop from 1.8s -> 780ms on canary. Good sign. Ramp to 50% over next 5m.
elena-oncall: Ramping to 50% now. Updating statuspage: add "Mitigation underway — routing changes applied; customers may see intermittent improvement."
maya-pm: Draft customer-facing note (short): "We are investigating increased response times for some API requests in US‑East. Engineers have applied routing mitigations; you may see intermittent improvements. We expect full recovery within 1 hour. We will follow up with a post-incident summary. — Redwood Inference" Thoughts?
ops-lead: Good. Add guidance: "If you rely on strict tail latency, consider retry/backoff (exponential) and pin to a dedicated region/Reserved capacity." Keep it short.
support-bot: Sending to affected accounts now with the note + link to status page.
elena-oncall: Ramp complete to 100% for affected traffic (traffic now served from warm pool) at 09:22 UTC. Monitoring.
ryan-sre: After full ramp p95 stabilized around 420ms, p99 ~1.1s (still elevated vs baseline). Throughput recovered. Looks like mitigations effective but we have residual tail.
alex-engr: Root cause theory: a recent kernel selector change on a small subset of nodes caused repeated fallback to a slower execution path under certain sequence-length distributions. We'll roll back the selector patch on those nodes and re-evaluate.
maya-pm: ETA to rollback & validate?
elena-oncall: Ops estimate ~25–35m to rollout patch rollback and confirm canary.
ops-lead: We should prepare postmortem/comms: initial summary + timeline + customer impact + RCA + follow-ups (rollback, better canary gating, perf test coverage). Maya please own external comms.
maya-pm: Will own. Will publish customer-facing incident summary after RCA. Draft internal template: "Summary, Impact (customers/orgs), Mitigation, Current Status, Next Steps, Owner(s)."
statuspage-bot: Status update posted: "Investigating — Increased latency in US‑East affecting a subset of requests. Mitigation applied; improvement observed. Follow-up update at 09:45 UTC." URL: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INF-LAT-USE1-001
elena-oncall: Handing over in 20m to @ryan-sre for overnight monitoring. Ryan, call if anything spikes again.
ryan-sre: Affirmative — I'll pick up at 09:42 UTC. I'll keep the routing policy in place until rollback confirmed.
support-bot: Sent follow-up messages to affected customers confirming mitigations and link to status. Some replies: one customer asked for SLA credit details — forwarding to sales-eng.
elena-oncall: New update: rollback started on 09:28 UTC to subset of nodes. Monitoring kernel fallback metric.
alex-engr: Rollback consistent on canary nodes, fallback metric down 90% on canary. Scheduling gradual rollout across pool; will pause if regressions.
elena-oncall: Noted a brief blink at 09:36 UTC where p99 jumped to 1.6s for ~2m during rollout step — paused and reverted that batch. We're taking slower progressive rollout.
ryan-sre: Logging the mitigation timeline and commands used in the incident runbook for handoff.
maya-pm: Preparing customer follow-up: "We identified and reverted a change to the inference kernel selector that caused slower fallback behavior on a subset of nodes. We rolled mitigations and expect full recovery within the hour. A post-incident report will follow." Sending when rollback fully complete.
statuspage-bot: Update posted at 09:45 UTC: "Monitoring — Mitigations applied and rollback underway; customers should see continued improvement. Next update by 10:15 UTC or as needed."
ops-lead: Good. Action items: (1) full rollback validation and perf baseline comparison, (2) increase canary gating for kernel-selector changes, (3) add perf regression test for int8 fallback case, (4) customer postmortem draft.
maya-pm: I'll create the external postmortem doc and cc engineering owners.
elena-oncall: Handoff complete at 09:42 UTC to @ryan-sre. I'll be available if needed.
ryan-sre: Monitoring in steady-state. Will close thread once rollback verified and statuspage moves to "resolved".
support-bot: Noting two customers requested SLA guidance; created tickets INC-1221 and INC-1222 and flagged for sales-eng.
statuspage-bot: Final update at 10:12 UTC: "Resolved — The root cause (kernel selector change) was reverted on affected nodes and we have verified performance has returned to normal baselines. No further action required for customers. A post-incident report will be posted in the next 48 hours." URL: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INF-LAT-USE1-001/postmortem
elena-oncall: Closing the incident. Thanks all for quick response. :tada:
maya-pm: Will publish postmortem doc in product/incidents and send customer summary.
ryan-sre: Leaving monitoring window open for 2 hours. If anything reappears reopen paging.
ops-lead: Great job. Let's ensure the rollout process is updated before next kernel-selector change.
sam-incident-bot: Incident INF-LAT-USE1-001 closed (duration ~1h10m)."
